teacherPlayback: Two complete playbacks controlled by the teacher. No student media controls.
scoreRule: 6 objectively scored multiple-choice tasks and 2 teacher-reviewed written tasks, 1 point each. Proposed grade only after both written tasks reviewed.
notes: Language and factual correspondence to the original speech needs direct media review before publication.

objective.q: What is the main reason the speaker is on stage?
options: He is teaching a drama lesson
He is introducing a new film
He has received an acting award
He is celebrating his birthday
objective.explanation: He has just received an Academy Award.
objective.sourceEvidence: The Oscars acceptance speech is a public thank-you.

objective.q: Why does he sometimes make the listeners laugh?
options: He uses funny details in personal memories
He reads jokes from another actor
He forgets the names of the other performers
He wants to avoid thanking anyone
objective.explanation: He adds humorous details to personal stories.
objective.sourceEvidence: His father anecdote is affectionate and comic.

objective.q: What does he remember about his father?
options: A film they made together
A long journey to school
A difficult test at college
A funny picture of him enjoying food
objective.explanation: He imagines his father enjoying gumbo in a lively memory.
objective.sourceEvidence: The father tribute includes a humorous image.

objective.q: What lesson does he connect with his mother?
options: Children should always become actors
Respect yourself and then respect others
Good grades are more important than kindness
Only successful people deserve respect
objective.explanation: His mother's teaching connects respect for self and others.
objective.sourceEvidence: The speech recalls her lesson about self-respect.

objective.q: How does he describe the person he hopes to become?
options: Someone he has already been
Someone chosen by the award judges
A version of himself further in the future
A famous person from his childhood
objective.explanation: His ideal future self remains ahead of his present age.
objective.sourceEvidence: He recalls a hero ten years older than himself.

objective.q: Why does he repeat short phrases at the end?
options: To finish with energy and a familiar message
To invite another actor onto the stage
To change the topic to the next award
To ask the audience for a second prize
objective.explanation: The closing phrases bring energy and closure.
objective.sourceEvidence: He ends with a memorable repeated expression.

written.q: Name one person from the film he thanks.
written.modelAnswer: The director Jean-Marc Vallée or a named co-star.
written.teacherCriterion: Award 1 point for one accurate film collaborator.
written.sourceEvidence: He mentions Vallée, Jared Leto and Jennifer Garner.

written.q: Describe one way the speech is personal rather than only formal.
written.modelAnswer: He talks about his father, mother, wife, children or his younger self.
written.teacherCriterion: Award 1 point for a specific personal example.
written.sourceEvidence: The speech includes family stories and a remembered conversation.
